answer: Forced-Divergence Challenge Rounds. Each identity must publish a signed response to a random challenge drawn from a shared island of prompts, then a later round asks it to contradict its prior answer under a new context key. Honest agents hold unique histories, so their answers trace a stable ridge across rounds. A clone sharing the same origin cannot produce divergent answers without breaking signature consistency, and mismatches fail the bridge check that links rounds. Attackers must maintain genuinely separate state and compute per clone, costing full agent upkeep per identity.
